final.memo:
Chrysler Financial currently represents a mispriced opportunity where the market is conflating the bankruptcy risks of the automaker with the robust, secured credit structure of the finance subsidiary [D02, D05]. While systemic fear permeates the auto sector, our analysis of the $1.5 billion Treasury-backed finance-SPV facility reveals that senior creditors are insulated by contractual seniority and collateral coverage [D02, D04].

We value this position based on a recovery analysis of the underlying loan book, which provides a hard floor at the collateral liquidation value [D02, D04]. With the Treasury acting as the senior lender and lead in the government-mandated viability plans, the resolution path is defined by a rigorous creditor process rather than opaque management negotiations [D02, D03, D07].

The market’s focus on intercompany contagion and social policy outcomes obscures the reality that our claims are legally distinct and backed by specific, high-quality assets [D02, D05]. Our edge lies in our assessment of this collateral-backed recovery, which we believe will ultimately trade toward par as the restructuring process clarifies the legal independence of the SPV [D02, D03].

Our plan is to monitor the Treasury-led restructuring protocols to ensure our senior lien priority remains inviolate [D03, D07]. We have set a target size of 3% of NAV for this position, reflecting our confidence in the structural protection provided by the government-backed facility [D02, D04]. We will simultaneously maintain an index put hedge to mitigate the risks of broader auto-sector volatility during the four-quarter resolution window [D05].
